title: Research: reduce selected BIT route interchange calls with paid permutation frames
body:
## Change and scope

Scoped construction and routing optimization. PR2915 restores field order around each reversed ADD, paying two complete B1 interchanges each time. This opt-in compiler carries the permutation through subsequent affine factors and pays for its final restoration. It returns validated factor words for the unchanged physical executor.

The actual selected registry's occurrence-weighted entrance/return invoice falls from **409,100,288 to 287,858,688 native calls (29.64%)**. All 1,123 source chart types, both orientations and 64 row copies are included. This is a finite route invoice, not execution of the full selected GL64 payload or a new recursive child profile.

The acceptance guard also prices the extra explicit-swap setup. Under the pinned, pending PR3301 complete traffic bound and the same-domain uniform B1 tariff, the complete local upper-bound expression is nonincreasing for every oriented chart. A control rejects a seven-to-five-call candidate whose setup/adapter coefficient increases. Every helper, copy, source access, emitted swap, native interval, intermediate clearance and final frame restoration remains paid within the stated local boundary.

Six complete baseline/optimized physical fixture pairs check 8,407 independent input columns, complete spectators, borrowed sources, owned outputs, occupied dirty scratch and cleanup. Active fixtures use 10–51% fewer physical Tape reads/writes/unit moves; the nine-ADD example falls from 72 to 8 native calls and 5,691,269 to 2,808,517 tape operations. The zero-high-width fixture is unchanged. These fixtures use elementary B1; fitted native/refinement, enclosing stock/backing and supplier admission remain open. No new kappa or default change is claimed.

## Verification

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/high-route-permutation-frames
```

The full registered replay passes on CPython 3.12.14 at frozen executable/certificate commit `14a8d05bd4215c451de7f62ce161ec36ffe12348`. The final head changes only VALIDATION.md and adds BENCHMARK.json. Algebra, controls and all physical comparisons also pass with assertions disabled from a read-only Git-free CPython 3.14.7 export. All 50 final package/input byte comparisons and 51 publication-export comparisons pass; final-export optimized controls pass too.

Three alternating fresh-process benchmark pairs on the same instrumented 486-bit fixture give median route time **3.671684 → 1.772378 seconds (2.07×)** and whole-process time **4.004344 → 2.107719 seconds (1.90×)**. Exact receipt hashes agree in every run. These measurements include provenance instrumentation and do not imply a full multiplication-runtime speedup.

The package includes the permutation proof, opt-in compiler, per-chart JSONL invoice, exact typed receipts, source pins and failure controls. Frozen predecessors, upstream/ and the selected record are unchanged. The per-chart certificate uses one JSONL row per source chart.

## Sources, overlap and credit

Base: `463113d675af7410ac91d53a4fed51ec6494eb9a`, priority revision 6, OS assignment seed 9. [Canonical claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2319#discussioncomment-19004969). The refreshed queue contains 375 open PRs and issue #913; the related fitted-native bridge claim is complementary. The earlier cached historical search covered 2,630 closed PRs and 2,076 Discussion records. Metadata searches are not a proof of novelty.

Jose Manuel supplied PR2915 (`fecc5a87574df441ddc3dad44f99fca9bd7fdd92`) and PR2899; David Arias supplied PR2753. Credit Nick Petalas's wrapper/prefix/scaling work, commdata2338/PR3233, Sagar Thakrar/PR3265, Krzysztof Wójt/PR3301 (`5ce521090c869211f808d132e28dcd4946f798c4`), Arham Tahir, ywz65 and the retained PR2157/PR589/PR555 lineage. The exact PR3301 proof is retained with attribution; its mathematical tariff is an explicit pending premise. Runtime source authentication does not require an unmerged Git object.

Tekalign (`tekuuu`), with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in derivation, implementation, verification and writing. Apache-2.0; no independent human or proof-assistant review claimed. Open next questions identify fitted-native admission and the enclosing caller ledger before default adoption.
